The swap deliberately leaves the new files at the old absolute paths on both platforms (Windows retires the locked files aside, Unix renames bin to bin.old), and the runtime resolves each assembly lazily on first touch, so the old process\\u0027s first load of any assembly it had not yet touched (Weasel.Postgresql, JasperFx.Events, whatever the store needs) comes from the new release. The only store open on the post-swap path is LiveGateGuard.FindOnThisNodeAsync (reached through WaitUnlessNowAsync\\u0027s delegate, then again from DaemonLifecycle.StopAsync), and it is inside catch (Exception); Program.cs also catches SchemaMigrationException and NpgsqlException and prints doctor advice, no trace. So the exception that reached Main is NOT the schema exception Windows remembered: it is most likely a load-time failure (TypeLoadException, MissingMethodException, FileLoadException, TypeInitializationException) raised while the runtime compiled FindOnThisNodeAsync itself, which lands at the delegate call site outside every try. After the swap the old process only launches the newly installed h9k as a child and relays its exit code. The child runs h9k daemon stop, h9k doctor --yes, h9k daemon start, in that order: start alone will not do, because DatabaseDoctor prompts on a terminal even with staleSchemaRepairedByCaller, and the daemon\\u0027s EventStoreSchemaGuard prints nothing on success. doctor --yes starts a stopped hall9k-postgres container without asking; inside --restart that is accepted and must be said in docs/operations.md. The point of no return is the child\\u0027s stop signal: before it, any failure leaves the old daemon running; after it, the command names the failed step and prints only the steps not yet done.
